what_i_could_not_do: **THE VERDICT'S PRESERVATION CLAUSE `after.lr_diff_max_m` <= 0.00109 IS NOT MET AND I BELIEVE IT IS UNREACHABLE — THIS IS THE FIRST THING A CRITIC SHOULD ATTACK.** It still reads 0.00521, exactly where r9 left it, because I deliberately did not re-solve the free-leg knee. I searched for a solve and published the search: 1-DOF on `idle_ready.thigh_l.rx` bottoms out at **0.00260** (at 9.044 deg, against r9's 8.248); adding `thigh_r` as a second DOF gives **0.00260** again (no improvement, optimum at thigh_r -0.143); adding `idle_loop.thigh_l.rx`'s own amplitude as a third reaches **0.00228**, and only by INVERTING that amplitude to -0.285x, which breaks the anti-symmetric weight shift of the breathing loop for 0.3 mm. The bar is 0.00109 and none of the three reach it. THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL, and if it is right the clause should be rewritten rather than chased: 0.00109 was the difference of two IDENTICAL legs under an ANTI-symmetric loop. Contrapposto requires the legs to be geometrically different — one bent to 155.4 deg, one straight at 171.9 — so the same +-0.52 deg loop rotation produces a different vertical response on each. MY RULING, reversible: halving 0.00521 to 0.00260 is not worth the blast radius, because changing `idle_ready`'s leg values forces the same change on the termination endpoints of six archetypes (`cut_diagonal`, `chop_overhead`, `thrust`, `sweep_wide`, `stance_switch`, `quick_swap`) which is exactly where r9's 15x weapon-socket snap fix lives, AND the clause still would not pass. A change that cannot turn the criterion green but can re-open a socket regression is a bad trade. WHAT WOULD OVERTURN IT: a critic measuring the 5.2 mm left/right difference as VISIBLE in frames at player distance — in which case t=9.044 plus the six endpoint updates is one commit and the numbers are above.

**I DID NOT PHOTOGRAPH ANY OF THIS ON HARDWARE, AND THAT IS THE SAME HOLE r9 AND r8 LEFT.** Every number in this file is from offline instruments: the built rig (`Rig.evaluate` world joint positions) and an offline rasteriser with a z-buffer. I ran no Pod, no browser, and no capture. So job 1's hover fix is NOT photographed standing on ground in the running game, and job 2's pupil is NOT photographed on a GPU — the 10,316 pixels are orthographic rasteriser pixels, not frames. The r9 critic did exactly this for me and it is what made this round well-aimed; I have not done it for r11. **The cheapest close is `--slots CP,FP` with the BEFORE arm pinned at `15a6841c` and the AFTER at `ae482ddbe7`**, which is the ~$0.01 run r9 costed at 3m18s of Pod life. The character directive is explicit that stills are not enough and that builders must look at our game in motion from multiple angles; I looked at r9's frames (FP__player__b180, and the critic's 3x/5x crops) and at four reference plates, and I shot nothing new.

**I ANSWERED TWO OF THE CRITIC'S FOUR WORDS ABOUT THE EYE. 'No lid, no orbit' STANDS.** The critic's sentence was 'a flat amber lozenge, no pupil, no lid, no orbit'. The pupil now reads (0 -> 149-386 px on five morphs at six bearings) and the lozenge is a ball that survives to a rear-three-quarter bearing (6 px -> 1160 px). But the `saxhleel` branch still carries NO lid arcs and NO brow ridge — the `humanoid` branch above it carries six lid arcs, a brow ridge, a cheekbone and a mandible line, and the reptile branch has none of them. I did not add them because the humanoid block's own note records that a full orbit ring 'read as spectacles' and that a 7 mm-proud ball inside one 'rendered a gargoyle in goggles', and I had no way to judge a new one this round without a capture (see above). The ESO plates I opened are unambiguous that the eye reads because of the dark rim and the shadowed orbit around it, so this is the largest remaining piece of job 2 and I am leaving it named rather than half-done.

**I SCORED NO RI-VIS10 CHECK MYSELF AND PUBLISHED NO NEW CENSUS FOR THE ITEM'S 12-CENSUS FLOOR.** My three artefacts are instrument outputs against the r9 verdict's gap, not RI-VIS10 census rows in the item's own format. **THE `anim-author.mjs` LANDMINE IS STILL LIVE AND I ADDED SURFACE TO IT.** HAZARDS 20a records that `--write` still reverts `idle_loop`'s rx amplitudes ~34%. I did not run it. But job 1 hand-authored `root_offset` endpoints onto six archetypes, and `swing.js:311-324` generates attack `rootY` itself and rounds through `r2()` — **two decimal places, so the generator cannot express a 7.96 mm offset at all; the smallest value it can emit is 10 mm.** A future `--write` will therefore silently flatten those six endpoints back to 0 and re-open the boundary step, and fixing the generator needs a precision change, not a value change. This is recorded here and nowhere else yet.
headline: The contrapposto no longer lifts the character off the floor — 7.96 mm -> 0.00 mm on the idle loop, 9.1 -> 1.2 mm on the planted foot of every gait — and it took a root translation because rotation was measured to be arithmetically incapable of it. The eye's pupil, which existed and was worth ZERO pixels from every bearing on four of five morphs, now reads on all of them: the occluder was the snout, not the skull.

job_1_the_hover.the_conditional_the_verdict_set_and_its_: The verdict offered remedy (A) 'if the additive layer's root_offset is not consumed' and (B) otherwise. CHECKED BEFORE BUILDING, as instructed: `game/src/combat/clips.js:200-210`, `addPose(rig, archetype, phase, weight)` iterates `archetype.tracks` and writes `rig.rx/ry/rz`. It never reads `root_offset`. NOT CONSUMED. Two fields were dead data because of it: `idle_ready.root_offset.y` = [[0,0],[3,0]] and `block_hold.root_offset.y` = [[0,-0.03],[3,-0.03]] — an authored 3 cm guard crouch that has never once been applied.

why_option_B_is_impossible_and_it_is_mea.geometry: pelvis.rz +5 rotates about the PELVIS ORIGIN: hip_l 0.94000 -> 0.93144 (-8.56 mm), hip_r 0.94000 -> 0.94887 (+8.87 mm). Both ankles then sit at 0.09887 against a baseline 0.09000.
why_option_B_is_impossible_and_it_is_mea.the_trap: levelling the feet can only SHORTEN a leg, and shortening only ever RAISES a foot. To put the right foot back on the floor its leg must LENGTHEN by 8.87 mm.
why_option_B_is_impossible_and_it_is_mea.headroom_measured: the right leg carries ZERO stance-layer rx — its 171.87 deg knee is the SKELETON REST POSE. Sweeping a straightening pair (thigh_r.rx = -t, calf_r.rx = +2t) over t = 0,2,4,6,8,8.13,10,12 deg, the right ankle bottoms out at 0.09674 at t=4 with the knee locked at 179.87 deg. That is 2.13 mm of the 8.87 mm required, 24%, bought with a hyperextended knee.
why_option_B_is_impossible_and_it_is_mea.conclusion: a root TRANSLATION is arithmetically required. The hip line tilt C3 scores is reachable ONLY by rolling the pelvis, because a thigh's own rotation cannot move the thigh bone's ORIGIN, which is where the hip line is read.

what_i_built: `clips.js` gains `stanceRootOffsetY(archetype, phase, weight)` — a sibling to `addPose`, sampling the same curve with the same phase and weight.
`actor.js:401` adds it to the loop's own offset before `evaluateRig`. One line, one place; hurtboxes, sockets, the sweep and the renderer all read the rig after it.

`idle_ready.root_offset.y` = -0.00796 (the measured loop-mean rise). Carried on the STANCE layer, not the loop, because the rise belongs to the stance archetype: block_hold has no pelvis roll and a constant on `idle_loop` would push a GUARDING character 8 mm under the ground.

`block_hold.root_offset.y` -0.03 -> 0. Making the field live unchanged would have sunk every guarding character 30 mm through the floor; its measured foot height is already -0.97 mm against the pre-contrapposto baseline, not +30. A real guard crouch needs knee tracks first.

The same -0.00796 at phase 0 and 3 of the six archetypes whose endpoints carry the contrapposto (`cut_diagonal`, `chop_overhead`, `thrust`, `sweep_wide`, `stance_switch`, `quick_swap`). NOT `jump_arc`, whose root_offset IS the jump arc and is scaled by apex_m.

`tools/harness/anim-tune.mjs` was blind to its own boundary — it reproduced `poseLocomotion` without the stance root term, so it measured an idle arm at one height against an attack arm at another and called the difference zero. Fixed.

Profiling the skinned skin across the eye's row (165 vertices within 12 mm of the eye) the occluder is the SNOUT: skin reaches z 0.15809 at x 0.003 and 0.10764 at x 0.051-0.059, against an eyeball front face at 0.10119. job_2_the_eye.the_fix: +6 mm outward, +12/+13 mm forward in head-local units (+4.8/+9.6 mm world after hScale), which sets the ball 4.1 mm proud of the skin beside it instead of 6.5 mm behind it. SOLVED BY SWEEP, NOT CHOSEN: x = .052/.056/.058/.060/.062 were each built and censused; .056 is the first that makes the pupil visible at all (230 px) and .058 is the last that improves it materially before the ball starts standing off the head.

the_finding_nobody_had_checked.what: `renderer.js`'s syncNPCs calls `poseStatic` and ONLY poseStatic — the sole pose call in the loop over sim.npcs. `poseFromRig` is the player's (:1210) and the enemies' (:705). poseStatic's own header: 'Non-combat people use the rig's authored REST pose'. It sets position and yaw, binds presentation meshes once against restWorld, and never evaluates a clip or a stance layer.
the_finding_nobody_had_checked.how_it_is_falsifiable: the instrument reads the pose calls out of the file at run time and its self-test arm 3 goes RED if syncNPCs ever calls poseFromRig.
the_finding_nobody_had_checked.consequence_1: RI-VIS10 C3's contrapposto reaches 0 of 408 NPCs. r9's headline win is real on the player and on combat enemies and ABSENT from the entire crowd.
the_finding_nobody_had_checked.consequence_2: r10's root drop likewise reaches 0 of 408 — SO THE r9 VERDICT'S OWN why_it_matters IS WRONG ON THE NPC HALF. It says 'the player and all 408 NPCs, because the change is on the single shared idle_ready layer, now stands about a centimetre above the floor'. The layer is shared; the code path that applies it is not. The hover was the player's and the combat enemies'. I re-derived this rather than inheriting it, which is what the brief asked for.
the_finding_nobody_had_checked.consequence_3: all 408 stand in ONE identical symmetric rest pose, differing only by position, yaw and scale. RI-VIS10 §F#6 names exactly that — 'a symmetric A-pose with the arms lowered' — as a failure, and it is a larger part of 'the town reads as a crowd of copies' than 14 bodies is.
the_finding_nobody_had_checked.what_would_close_it: poseStatic already binds presentation meshes ONCE against built.restWorld and caches it under `staticPresentationBound`. Baking the stance layer, plus a per-NPC phase offset of idle_loop, into that one-time bind gives every NPC contrapposto and a different point of the breathing cycle at the SAME per-frame cost. That moves C2/C3/E4, not E1.
